### Set Plugin Installation Setting

- Signature: `client.beta.organization.plugins.installationSettings.set(target: string, params: InstallationSettingSetParams, options?: RequestOptions): BetaPluginInstallationSetting`
- Endpoint: `POST /v1/organizations/plugins/{plugin_id}/installation_settings/{target}`
- Beta header: `anthropic-beta: ce-plugins-2026-09-01`

Set or change an organization-owned Plugin's installation setting for the whole
organization or for one RBAC Group.

Writing the value a target already holds of its own changes nothing.

A member-owned Plugin has shares instead of installation settings, so this path
returns 404 for one.

Send a Plugin's installation-setting writes one at a time. If several writes for the
same Plugin arrive at the same time, the server handles them one after another and
can answer some of them with `503` instead of applying them. That `503` carries
`x-should-retry: true`, and the write is safe to repeat: wait a second or two, then
send it again.

**Accepted credentials:** an Admin API key with the `write:plugins` scope.

Every request must include the beta header `anthropic-beta: ce-plugins-2026-09-01`. A request without it returns `404`, exactly as if the endpoint did not exist. The Plugins API is in beta and is available to Claude Enterprise organizations only. It is not available to Claude Platform (Claude Console) organizations, or to organizations with HIPAA readiness enabled.

```ts
const client = new Anthropic({
  apiKey: process.env["ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"] // This is the default and can be omitted
});

const betaPluginInstallationSetting =
  await client.beta.organization.plugins.installationSettings.set("target", {
    plugin_id: "plugin_id",
    installation_preference: "required"
  });

console.log(betaPluginInstallationSetting.plugin_id);
```

```json
  "updated_at": "2026-03-14T09:26:53.589793Z"
}
```

Writing the `organization` target stops the Plugin from inheriting its marketplace's default, even when the value written equals that default. */

### Remove Plugin Installation Setting

- Signature: `client.beta.organization.plugins.installationSettings.remove(target: string, params: InstallationSettingRemoveParams, options?: RequestOptions): BetaDeletedPluginInstallationSetting`
- Endpoint: `DELETE /v1/organizations/plugins/{plugin_id}/installation_settings/{target}`
- Beta header: `anthropic-beta: ce-plugins-2026-09-01`

Remove an organization-owned Plugin's own installation setting for the whole
organization or for one RBAC Group.

Removing the `organization` target returns the Plugin to its marketplace's default
installation setting and leaves the groups' settings in place. Removing a group's
setting makes the group's members fall back to the Plugin's organization-wide setting
or to the settings of their other groups.

A target that holds no setting of its own returns 404 (a Plugin that already inherits
its marketplace's default holds no `organization` setting), and so does a member-owned
Plugin.

A removal counts as one of the Plugin's installation-setting writes: send all of those
writes one at a time. If several arrive for the same Plugin at the same time, the server
handles them one after another and can answer some of them with `503` and
`x-should-retry: true` instead of applying them; wait a second or two and send the
removal again. A `404` on the repeat means the setting is already gone.

**Accepted credentials:** an Admin API key with the `write:plugins` scope.

Every request must include the beta header `anthropic-beta: ce-plugins-2026-09-01`. A request without it returns `404`, exactly as if the endpoint did not exist. The Plugins API is in beta and is available to Claude Enterprise organizations only. It is not available to Claude Platform (Claude Console) organizations, or to organizations with HIPAA readiness enabled.

#### Example request

```ts
import Anthropic from "@anthropic-ai/sdk";

const client = new Anthropic({
  apiKey: process.env["ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"] // This is the default and can be omitted
});

const betaDeletedPluginInstallationSetting =
  await client.beta.organization.plugins.installationSettings.remove("target", {
    plugin_id: "plugin_id"
  });

console.log(betaDeletedPluginInstallationSetting.plugin_id);
```

#### Example response (200)

```json
{
  "plugin_id": "plugin_01JyHfbRkZvD1gW7oTqXc3Ne",
  "target": {
    "rbac_group_id": "rbac_group_012rppKaSVsmTo6NqRDXQXNF",
    "type": "rbac_group"
  },
  "type": "plugin_installation_setting_deleted"
}
```

#### Parameters

```ts
/** The target whose own setting is removed: the literal `organization` for the Plugin's organization-wide setting, or an RBAC Group's ID (prefixed `rbac_group_`) for that group's own setting. Removing the `organization` setting returns the Plugin to its marketplace's default. */
target: string; // path parameter

interface InstallationSettingRemoveParams {
  /** ID of the Plugin (prefixed `plugin_`). */
  plugin_id: string; // path parameter
  /** This endpoint is in beta: requests must send `ce-plugins-2026-09-01` in this header. */
  betas?: Array<AnthropicBeta>; // header parameter
}
```

#### Returns

```ts

  /** Always `plugin_installation_setting_deleted`. */
  type: "plugin_installation_setting_deleted";
  /** The Plugin's ID. */
  plugin_id: string;
  /** Whose setting was removed. */
  target: BetaPluginTargetOrganization | BetaPluginTargetRBACGroup | BetaPluginTargetOrganizationMember;
}
```

### Validate Plugin Marketplace Repository

- Signature: `client.beta.organization.pluginMarketplaces.validateRepository(params: PluginMarketplaceValidateRepositoryParams, options?: RequestOptions): BetaPluginMarketplaceValidationReport`
- Endpoint: `POST /v1/organizations/plugin_marketplaces/validate_repository`
- Beta header: `anthropic-beta: ce-plugins-2026-09-01`

Check whether a plugin marketplace held in a public GitHub repository would
synchronize into claude.ai, without connecting or storing it.

To check a `.zip` of the marketplace directory instead, use Validate Plugin Marketplace Archive.

The report says whether `marketplace.json` is well-formed, which plugins a
synchronization would skip and why, and which plugins would synchronize only in
part, with some files left out. A repository that is missing, private, or has no such branch or commit is reported, not refused: the response is a report with `valid: false`. Plugin sources outside the marketplace
are fetched anonymously from GitHub, so a private one is reported as not found or as
needing a GitHub sign-in; a source on any other host is not fetched here, and the
report notes that it will be checked when the marketplace actually synchronizes.

Nothing is recorded on the Compliance API activity feed.

For a worked example, see [Validate marketplace content](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/plugins-api?sdk_languages=typescript#validate-marketplace-content)
in the Plugins API guide.

**Accepted credentials:** an Admin API key with the `read:plugins` or `write:plugins` scope; `read:org_audit` and `read:compliance_org_data` do not grant it.

Every request must include the beta header `anthropic-beta: ce-plugins-2026-09-01`. A request without it returns `404`, exactly as if the endpoint did not exist. The Plugins API is in beta and is available to Claude Enterprise organizations only. It is not available to Claude Platform (Claude Console) organizations, or to organizations with HIPAA readiness enabled.

#### Example request

```ts
import Anthropic from "@anthropic-ai/sdk";

const client = new Anthropic({
  apiKey: process.env["ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"] // This is the default and can be omitted
});

const betaPluginMarketplaceValidationReport =
  await client.beta.organization.pluginMarketplaces.validateRepository({

console.log(betaPluginMarketplaceValidationReport.valid);
```

```ts
interface PluginMarketplaceValidateRepositoryParams {
  /** The `https://` URL of a public repository on github.com that holds the marketplace. A URL longer than 2,048 characters, on any other host or scheme, with a port other than 443 or 80, with credentials in it, or that does not name exactly `owner/repo` (a trailing `.git` or `/` is accepted) is a 400. A private or missing repository is reported in the response, not refused. */
  repository_url: string; // minLength: 1
  /** The branch to validate the tip of, or the full 40-character SHA of the commit to validate. When omitted, the branch a synchronization would read (usually the repository's default branch); if that is not the default branch, the report's `ref` says which branch was read. An empty string, a value longer than 255 characters, or one that contains `..` or a character other than ASCII letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-`, `+`, and `/`, is a 400. Any other value that is not a 40-character SHA is read as a branch name; if the repository has no such branch, the response is a report with `valid: false`, not a 400. */
  ref?: string | null; // minLength: 1
```

#### Returns

```ts
/** The outcome of validating plugin marketplace content: a report, not a stored object, so nothing in it can be retrieved afterwards. */
interface BetaPluginMarketplaceValidationReport {
  /** Always `plugin_marketplace_validation_report`. */
  type: "plugin_marketplace_validation_report";
  /** The full SHA of the commit that was validated: for a repository, the commit that was read; for an uploaded archive, the commit recorded in the archive's comment (as a Git host's download writes it; not verified), else null. */
  commit_sha: string | null;
  /** Set when nothing could be validated: the repository or archive could not be read, or marketplace.json is missing, malformed or over a limit. Null otherwise. */
  manifest_error: string | null;
  /** A stable identifier for `manifest_error`; null when that is. */
  manifest_error_code: string | null;
  /** One entry per plugin a synchronization would skip entirely, keyed by the plugin's name in marketplace.json. */
  plugin_errors: Array<BetaPluginMarketplaceValidationPluginError>;
  /** One entry per plugin that would synchronize with some of its contents left out, keyed by the plugin's name in marketplace.json. */
  plugin_warnings: Array<BetaPluginMarketplaceValidationPluginWarnings>;
  /** For a repository, the branch that was read by name: the one requested, or else the branch a synchronization of this repository is set to read. Null when no branch is named or set and the repository's default branch was read, for a request by commit SHA, and for an uploaded archive. */
  ref: string | null;
  /** How many plugins marketplace.json declares; 0 when it could not be read. */
  total_plugin_count: number;
  /** True when marketplace.json is well-formed and no plugin would be skipped; warnings never make it false. */
  valid: boolean;
}
```

#### Types

```ts
interface BetaPluginMarketplaceValidationPluginError {

  error: string;

  /** The plugin's name, as its entry in marketplace.json declares it. */
  name: string;
}

interface BetaPluginMarketplaceValidationPluginWarnings {
  /** The plugin's name, as its entry in marketplace.json declares it. */
  name: string;
  /** The parts of the plugin a synchronization would leave out. */
  warnings: Array<BetaPluginMarketplaceValidationPluginWarning>;
}

interface BetaPluginMarketplaceValidationPluginWarning {
  /** A stable identifier for the kind of warning. */
  error_code: string;
  /** What would be left out, and why. */
  message: string;
}
```

### Validate Plugin Marketplace Archive

- Signature: `client.beta.organization.pluginMarketplaces.validateArchive(params: PluginMarketplaceValidateArchiveParams, options?: RequestOptions): BetaPluginMarketplaceValidationReport`
- Endpoint: `POST /v1/organizations/plugin_marketplaces/validate_archive`
- Beta header: `anthropic-beta: ce-plugins-2026-09-01`

Check whether a plugin marketplace, uploaded as a `.zip` of the marketplace
directory, would synchronize into claude.ai, without connecting or storing it.

To check a public GitHub repository instead, use Validate Plugin Marketplace Repository.

The report says whether `marketplace.json` is well-formed, which plugins a
synchronization would skip and why, and which plugins would synchronize only in
part, with some files left out. An archive that cannot be read as a marketplace is reported, not refused: the response is a report with `valid: false`. Plugin sources outside the marketplace
are fetched anonymously from GitHub, so a private one is reported as not found or as
needing a GitHub sign-in; a source on any other host is not fetched here, and the
report notes that it will be checked when the marketplace actually synchronizes.

Nothing is recorded on the Compliance API activity feed.

For a worked example, see [Validate marketplace content](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/plugins-api?sdk_languages=typescript#validate-marketplace-content)
in the Plugins API guide.

**Accepted credentials:** an Admin API key with the `read:plugins` or `write:plugins` scope; `read:org_audit` and `read:compliance_org_data` do not grant it.

Every request must include the beta header `anthropic-beta: ce-plugins-2026-09-01`. A request without it returns `404`, exactly as if the endpoint did not exist. The Plugins API is in beta and is available to Claude Enterprise organizations only. It is not available to Claude Platform (Claude Console) organizations, or to organizations with HIPAA readiness enabled.

#### Example request

```ts
import fs from "fs";
import Anthropic from "@anthropic-ai/sdk";

const client = new Anthropic({
  apiKey: process.env["ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"] // This is the default and can be omitted
});

const betaPluginMarketplaceValidationReport =
  await client.beta.organization.pluginMarketplaces.validateArchive({
    archive: fs.createReadStream("path/to/file")
  });

console.log(betaPluginMarketplaceValidationReport.valid);
```

#### Example response (200)

```json
{
  "commit_sha": "9fceb02d0ae598e95dc970b74767f19372d61af8",
  "manifest_error": "manifest_error",
  "manifest_error_code": "marketplace_sync_manifest_not_found",
  "plugin_errors": [
    {
      "error": "error",
      "error_code": "marketplace_sync_plugin_missing_manifest",
      "name": "name"
    }
  ],
  "plugin_warnings": [
    {
      "name": "name",
      "warnings": [
        {
          "error_code": "marketplace_sync_zipball_symlink_dangling",
          "message": "message"
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "ref": "main",
  "total_plugin_count": 0,
  "type": "plugin_marketplace_validation_report",
  "valid": false
}
```

#### Parameters

```ts
interface PluginMarketplaceValidateArchiveParams {
  /** A .zip of the marketplace directory (its contents at the root, or wrapped in one folder as a Git host's download produces), sent as a file part with a filename; DEFLATE- or STORE-compressed, at most 32 MB. A part sent without a filename, a second archive part, or any other form field is a 400; a larger archive is a 413. */
  archive: Uploadable; // format: binary
  /** This endpoint is in beta: requests must send `ce-plugins-2026-09-01` in this header. */
  betas?: Array<AnthropicBeta>; // header parameter
}
```

#### Errors

Any method can also return the general [HTTP errors](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/errors?sdk_languages=typescript).

- `BetaUnsupportedCharsetError` (HTTP status 400, error code `unsupported_charset`)

  The request's `Content-Type` header names a charset other than UTF-8, ISO-8859-1 or US-ASCII. Send the request with no charset, or with one of these.

## Beta › Organization › Telemetry Destinations

### Create a Telemetry Destination

- Signature: `client.beta.organization.telemetryDestinations.create(params: TelemetryDestinationCreateParams, options?: RequestOptions): BetaTelemetryDestination`
- Endpoint: `POST /v1/organizations/telemetry_destinations`
- Beta header: `anthropic-beta: telemetry-destinations-2026-08-11`

Register an OpenTelemetry destination for the organization.

The destination starts in state `enabled`. An organization can have at most 10 destinations, including disabled ones.

See the [OpenTelemetry export guide](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/opentelemetry?sdk_languages=typescript#add-a-destination) to learn more about adding a destination.

#### Example request

```ts
import Anthropic from "@anthropic-ai/sdk";

const client = new Anthropic({
  apiKey: process.env["ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"] // This is the default and can be omitted
});

const betaTelemetryDestination = await client.beta.organization.telemetryDestinations.create({
  endpoint_url: "x",
  workspaces: { type: "all" }
});

console.log(betaTelemetryDestination.id);
```

#### Example response (200)

```json
{
  "id": "id",
  "created_at": "2019-12-27T18:11:19.117Z",
  "delivery_health": {
    "last_error": "last_error",
    "last_error_at": "2019-12-27T18:11:19.117Z",
    "last_success_at": "2019-12-27T18:11:19.117Z"
  },
  "display_name": "display_name",
  "endpoint_url": "endpoint_url",
  "header_names": [
    "string"
  ],
  "state": {
    "type": "enabled"
  },
  "traces": {
    "content_mode": "metadata_only",
    "enabled": true,
    "endpoint_url": "endpoint_url",
    "max_content_bytes": 0
  },
  "type": "telemetry_destination",
  "updated_at": "2019-12-27T18:11:19.117Z",
  "workspaces": {
    "type": "all"
  }
}
```

#### Parameters

```ts
interface TelemetryDestinationCreateParams {
  /** The base URL of your collector's OTLP/HTTP endpoint, for example `https://gateway.example.com`. The URL must use `https` and a hostname, not an IP address. The port, if given, must be 443. The URL must not contain a query string, a fragment, or a username and password. At most 2,048 characters. A path prefix, such as `/otlp`, is allowed. Don't include the per-signal path (`/v1/traces`), because the API appends it on delivery. If your collector takes traces on another path, also set `traces.endpoint_url`. */
  endpoint_url: string; // minLength: 1, maxLength: 2048
  /** Which of the organization's workspaces the destination covers. */
  workspaces: BetaTelemetryDestinationWorkspacesParams;
  /** Human-readable name for the destination. Optional. 1 to 255 characters. */
  display_name?: string | null;
  /** Request headers that the API sends with every delivery, typically your collector's authentication header (for example `authorization`). The API never returns the values. Reads show only `header_names`. At most 20 headers. Names are at most 128 characters. Two names can't differ only in case. Values are printable ASCII, at most 4,096 characters, and can't begin or end with a space. Names and values together are at most 16,384 bytes. Reserved names are rejected, for example `host`, `cookie`, `user-agent`, and names that start with `content-`, `proxy-`, `x-forwarded-`, or `anthropic-`. For this check, `_` in a name counts as `-`. */
  headers?: Record<string, string>;
  /** The settings for the traces that the destination receives. If you leave it out, every setting takes its default. */
  traces?: BetaTelemetryDestinationTracesParams;
  /** This endpoint is in beta: requests must send `telemetry-destinations-2026-08-11` in this header. */
  betas?: Array<AnthropicBeta>; // header parameter
}
```

#### Returns

```ts
/** An OpenTelemetry destination: an OTLP/HTTP endpoint, the request headers sent with every delivery to it, what the exported spans contain, and which workspaces it covers. A destination belongs to an organization. A workspace's spans go to every enabled destination that covers it. */
interface BetaTelemetryDestination {
  type: "telemetry_destination";
  /** The unique ID of the destination (`tdst_...`). */
  id: string;
  /** Time the destination was created. */
  created_at: string; // format: date-time
  /** The most recent delivery results for this destination. */
  delivery_health: BetaTelemetryDestinationDeliveryHealth;
  /** Human-readable name for the destination. Null when none was set. */
  display_name: string | null;
  /** The base URL of the destination's OTLP/HTTP endpoint, exactly as registered. The API appends the per-signal path, such as `/v1/traces`, on delivery, unless `traces.endpoint_url` is set. */
  endpoint_url: string;
  /** Names of the registered request headers. Header values are write-only and are never returned. */
  header_names: Array<string>;
  /** Whether the destination receives deliveries. */
  state: BetaTelemetryDestinationState;
  /** The destination's settings for the traces it receives. */
  traces: BetaTelemetryDestinationTraces;
  /** Time of the last change to the destination's configuration or state. Changes to `delivery_health` don't change it. An update that sets a header value always changes it, even when the value is the same as before. Adding or removing a single workspace on the destination's list doesn't change it. An update that changes the list does. */
  updated_at: string; // format: date-time
  /** Which of the organization's workspaces the destination covers. */
  workspaces: BetaTelemetryDestinationWorkspaces;
}
```

#### Types

```ts
type BetaTelemetryDestinationWorkspacesParams = BetaTelemetryDestinationWorkspacesAllParams | BetaTelemetryDestinationWorkspacesIncludeParams | BetaTelemetryDestinationWorkspacesExcludeParams;

interface BetaTelemetryDestinationTracesParams {
  /** What the exported spans contain. Defaults to `metadata_only` on create. On update, `null` sets `metadata_only`. */
  content_mode?: BetaTelemetryDestinationContentMode | null;
  /** Whether the destination receives traces. Defaults to true on create. It cannot be null. */
  enabled?: boolean;
  /** The full URL of your collector's traces endpoint, for a collector that takes traces on a path other than `/v1/traces`. The API posts traces to it exactly as given and appends nothing. The same rules as for `endpoint_url` apply, except that any path is allowed. It must have the same scheme, host, and port as `endpoint_url`. At most 2,048 characters. On create, `null` is the same as leaving it out. On update, `null` removes it. The API then posts traces to `endpoint_url` with `/v1/traces` appended. A change of this URL alone keeps the registered headers. */
  endpoint_url?: string | null; // maxLength: 2048
  /** The most bytes of content that one exported span can contain, from 1 up to the API's maximum. `null` sets no bound, so only the API's maximum applies. On create, leaving it out is the same as `null`. The error for a value above the maximum states the maximum. */
  max_content_bytes?: number | null; // format: int32
}

interface BetaTelemetryDestinationDeliveryHealth {
  /** A message that describes the most recent failed delivery to the destination, or `null` if no delivery has failed yet. Examples are `temporary DNS failure`, `TLS failure`, `timeout`, `connection failure`, `invalid address`, `HTTP error (status 503)`, and `redirect (status 301)`. The message is `invalid address` both for a hostname that doesn't exist and for an address that isn't publicly routable. It never contains the endpoint's response body, a header value, a network address, or TLS details. `last_error` and `last_error_at` always change together. A later successful delivery doesn't clear them. If `last_success_at` is later than `last_error_at`, a delivery has succeeded since this failure. See the [OpenTelemetry export guide](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/opentelemetry?sdk_languages=typescript#delivery-errors) to learn the likely cause of each error. */
  last_error: string | null;
  /** Time of the failure that `last_error` describes. Changes together with `last_error`. Null until a delivery first fails. */
  last_error_at: string | null; // format: date-time
  /** Time of the most recent successful delivery to the destination, or `null` if no delivery has succeeded yet. */
  last_success_at: string | null; // format: date-time
}

type BetaTelemetryDestinationState = BetaTelemetryDestinationStateEnabled | BetaTelemetryDestinationStateDisabled;

interface BetaTelemetryDestinationTraces {
  /** What the exported spans contain. */
  content_mode: BetaTelemetryDestinationContentMode;
  /** Whether the destination receives traces. A destination whose `enabled` is false keeps its other settings. */
  enabled: boolean;
  /** The full URL that the API posts traces to, exactly as registered, or `null` if the destination doesn't have one. When it is `null`, the API posts traces to `endpoint_url` with `/v1/traces` appended. */
  endpoint_url: string | null;
  /** The most bytes of content that one exported span can contain, or `null` if only the API's maximum applies. Content means model prompts and responses, and tool inputs and outputs. The API shortens longer content to this size before it delivers the span. A destination whose `content_mode` is `metadata_only` keeps this value. It applies once `content_mode` is `content`. */
  max_content_bytes: number | null; // format: int32
}

type BetaTelemetryDestinationWorkspaces = BetaTelemetryDestinationWorkspacesAll | BetaTelemetryDestinationWorkspacesInclude | BetaTelemetryDestinationWorkspacesExclude;

/** Cover every workspace of the organization. Doesn't take `workspace_ids`. An update that sets `all` empties the destination's workspace list. */
interface BetaTelemetryDestinationWorkspacesAllParams {
  type: "all";
}

/** Cover only the workspaces on the list. */
interface BetaTelemetryDestinationWorkspacesIncludeParams {
  type: "include";
  /** The IDs of the workspaces on the destination's list (`wrkspc_...`). At most 100 per request. On create, these workspaces become the destination's list. If you leave `workspace_ids` out, the list starts empty. If the API refuses one of the IDs, it doesn't create the destination. On update, `workspace_ids` replaces the whole list. A workspace that stays on the list keeps its entry and its `created_at`. An empty array empties the list. If you leave `workspace_ids` out and the type stays the same, the list doesn't change. If you leave it out and the type changes, the new list starts empty. After a change to `include` without `workspace_ids`, the destination doesn't cover any workspace until one is added. After a change to `exclude` without `workspace_ids`, it covers every workspace. An ID sent more than once is added once. An archived workspace can't be added to a list. An update can keep an archived workspace that is already on the list. */
  workspace_ids?: Array<string>;
}

/** Cover every workspace of the organization except the workspaces on the list. */
interface BetaTelemetryDestinationWorkspacesExcludeParams {
  type: "exclude";
  /** The IDs of the workspaces on the destination's list (`wrkspc_...`). At most 100 per request. On create, these workspaces become the destination's list. If you leave `workspace_ids` out, the list starts empty. If the API refuses one of the IDs, it doesn't create the destination. On update, `workspace_ids` replaces the whole list. A workspace that stays on the list keeps its entry and its `created_at`. An empty array empties the list. If you leave `workspace_ids` out and the type stays the same, the list doesn't change. If you leave it out and the type changes, the new list starts empty. After a change to `include` without `workspace_ids`, the destination doesn't cover any workspace until one is added. After a change to `exclude` without `workspace_ids`, it covers every workspace. An ID sent more than once is added once. An archived workspace can't be added to a list. An update can keep an archived workspace that is already on the list. */
  workspace_ids?: Array<string>;
}

type BetaTelemetryDestinationContentMode =
  /** The spans contain identifiers, timing, status, token counts, and similar metadata. They don't contain prompt text, completion text, or tool inputs and outputs. */
  | "metadata_only"
  /** The spans contain the same metadata as `metadata_only`, plus message and tool content. An organization with a data-handling restriction, such as under HIPAA, can't choose this mode. The API exports only metadata for such an organization, even to a destination that already has `content`. */
  | "content";

/** The destination covers every workspace of the organization, including the default workspace, archived workspaces, and workspaces created later. It doesn't have a list. */
interface BetaTelemetryDestinationWorkspacesAll {
  type: "all";
}

/** The destination covers the workspaces on its list, and no others. */
interface BetaTelemetryDestinationWorkspacesInclude {
  type: "include";
}

/** The destination covers every workspace of the organization except the workspaces on its list. A workspace created later is covered until it is added to the list. */
interface BetaTelemetryDestinationWorkspacesExclude {
  type: "exclude";
}

/** The telemetry destination receives the spans of the workspaces that it covers. */
interface BetaTelemetryDestinationStateEnabled {
  type: "enabled";
}

/** The API doesn't deliver anything to the telemetry destination. Spans produced while it is disabled aren't delivered later. */
interface BetaTelemetryDestinationStateDisabled {
  type: "disabled";
  /** Whether a caller or the API disabled the destination and, when the API did, why. Read-only. */
  reason: BetaTelemetryDestinationDisabledReason;
}

type BetaTelemetryDestinationDisabledReason = BetaTelemetryDestinationDisabledReasonCaller | BetaTelemetryDestinationDisabledReasonSustainedFailure | BetaTelemetryDestinationDisabledReasonInvalidAddress | BetaTelemetryDestinationDisabledReasonRedirect;

/** A caller disabled the destination with an update that set `state` to `disabled`. */
interface BetaTelemetryDestinationDisabledReasonCaller {
  type: "caller";
}

/** The API disabled the destination because deliveries to it failed, with no successful delivery in between, for longer than a threshold that Anthropic configures and that is not part of this contract. The reason is `invalid_address` instead when the most recent failed delivery failed with an invalid address. */
interface BetaTelemetryDestinationDisabledReasonSustainedFailure {
  type: "sustained_failure";
}

/** The API disabled the destination because deliveries to it failed for longer than the same threshold as for `sustained_failure`, and the most recent failed delivery failed with an invalid address: the DNS answer says that the endpoint's hostname doesn't exist or doesn't have an address, or the address that the API would connect to isn't publicly routable or is reserved, for example a loopback, link-local, private-network, or cloud-metadata address. The API doesn't connect to such an address, and retries the delivery a bounded number of times as it does after a timeout. A timeout or a server failure of the DNS lookup is a temporary DNS failure instead, not an invalid address. */
interface BetaTelemetryDestinationDisabledReasonInvalidAddress {
  type: "invalid_address";
}

/** The API disabled the destination because the endpoint answered a delivery with a 3xx status. Redirects are never followed, and one such answer disables the destination at once. */
interface BetaTelemetryDestinationDisabledReasonRedirect {
  type: "redirect";
}
```

### Update a Telemetry Destination

- Signature: `client.beta.organization.telemetryDestinations.update(destinationID: string, params: TelemetryDestinationUpdateParams, options?: RequestOptions): BetaTelemetryDestination`
- Endpoint: `POST /v1/organizations/telemetry_destinations/{destination_id}`
- Beta header: `anthropic-beta: telemetry-destinations-2026-08-11`

Change a telemetry destination's settings, its state, or which workspaces it covers.

Send at least one field. Omitted fields keep their stored values, except the registered headers, which a change of the endpoint's hostname or port removes. Only `display_name`, `traces`, `traces.endpoint_url`, `traces.content_mode`, `traces.max_content_bytes`, and individual `headers` values accept `null`.

If another request changes the destination while the update runs, the API returns a 409 `conflict_error`. Read the destination again, then retry the update.

See the [OpenTelemetry export guide](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/opentelemetry?sdk_languages=typescript#delivery-and-health) to learn more about changing a destination.

#### Example request

```ts
import Anthropic from "@anthropic-ai/sdk";

const client = new Anthropic({
  apiKey: process.env["ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"] // This is the default and can be omitted
});

const betaTelemetryDestination = await client.beta.organization.telemetryDestinations.update(
  "destination_id",
  {}
);

console.log(betaTelemetryDestination.id);
```

#### Example response (200)

```json
{
  "id": "id",
  "created_at": "2019-12-27T18:11:19.117Z",
  "delivery_health": {
    "last_error": "last_error",
    "last_error_at": "2019-12-27T18:11:19.117Z",
    "last_success_at": "2019-12-27T18:11:19.117Z"
  },
  "display_name": "display_name",
  "endpoint_url": "endpoint_url",
  "header_names": [
    "string"
  ],
  "state": {
    "type": "enabled"
  },
  "traces": {
    "content_mode": "metadata_only",
    "enabled": true,
    "endpoint_url": "endpoint_url",
    "max_content_bytes": 0
  },
  "type": "telemetry_destination",
  "updated_at": "2019-12-27T18:11:19.117Z",
  "workspaces": {
    "type": "all"
  }
}
```

#### Parameters

```ts
/** ID of the destination (`tdst_...`). */
destinationID: string; // path parameter

interface TelemetryDestinationUpdateParams {
  /** New human-readable name, 1 to 255 characters. Null clears it. */
  display_name?: string | null;
  /** The new base URL of the destination's OTLP/HTTP endpoint. The same rules as on create apply. A change of hostname or port first removes every registered header, so send the headers for the new endpoint in the same request. When the destination has a `traces.endpoint_url`, such a change must also set `traces.endpoint_url` to a URL with the new hostname and port, or to `null`. A change of the path alone keeps the headers. */
  endpoint_url?: string; // maxLength: 2048
  /** Headers to set or remove. The API merges them into the destination's headers by name. Names compare case-insensitively. A string value sets or replaces that header. A `null` value removes it. Headers that you omit don't change. The field itself can't be `null`. A request that sets a header value must also include `endpoint_url`. The current URL is accepted. The resulting set must stay within the same limits as on create. When the request sets a value, each stored value that it doesn't set counts as 4,096 bytes toward the 16,384-byte limit, because you can't read its real length. So to change one header of a destination that has four or more other headers, send the values of the others again in the same request. */
  headers?: Record<string, string | null> | null;
  /** Whether the destination receives deliveries after the update. The field can't be `null`. */
  state?: BetaTelemetryDestinationStateParams;
  /** The traces settings to change. Omitted settings keep their stored values. `null` sets every traces setting to its create default. */
  traces?: BetaTelemetryDestinationTracesParams | null;
  /** The new workspace scope, in the same form as on create. The field can't be `null`. The API refuses an update that changes the type or sends `workspace_ids` while the destination's list has more than 750 workspaces. Remove workspaces one at a time until 750 or fewer remain, then send the update again. */
  workspaces?: BetaTelemetryDestinationWorkspacesParams;
  /** This endpoint is in beta: requests must send `telemetry-destinations-2026-08-11` in this header. */
  betas?: Array<AnthropicBeta>; // header parameter
}
```

#### Types

```ts
type BetaTelemetryDestinationStateParams = BetaTelemetryDestinationStateEnabledParams | BetaTelemetryDestinationStateDisabledParams;

/** Start deliveries to the telemetry destination again. This doesn't reset `delivery_health`. */
interface BetaTelemetryDestinationStateEnabledParams {
  type: "enabled";
}

/** Stop deliveries to the telemetry destination. Spans produced while it is disabled aren't delivered later. A destination that is already disabled keeps its `reason`. */
interface BetaTelemetryDestinationStateDisabledParams {
  type: "disabled";
}
```

### Test a Telemetry Destination

- Signature: `client.beta.organization.telemetryDestinations.test(destinationID: string, params?: TelemetryDestinationTestParams, options?: RequestOptions): BetaTelemetryDestinationTestResponse`
- Endpoint: `POST /v1/organizations/telemetry_destinations/{destination_id}/test`
- Beta header: `anthropic-beta: telemetry-destinations-2026-08-11`

Send one test span, named `anthropic.test`, to the destination with its registered headers, once and without retries, and report the destination's answer. The response is 200 whether or not the destination answered with a 2xx status: its `result` has the type `success`, or the type `failure` and the reason in `error`. The destination's configuration, `state` and `delivery_health` do not change. A disabled destination can be tested too. Wait 10 seconds between tests of one destination; a request that comes sooner may be answered with status 429.

#### Example request

```ts
import Anthropic from "@anthropic-ai/sdk";

const client = new Anthropic({
  apiKey: process.env["ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"] // This is the default and can be omitted
});

const betaTelemetryDestinationTestResponse =
  await client.beta.organization.telemetryDestinations.test("destination_id");

console.log(betaTelemetryDestinationTestResponse.result);
```

#### Example response (200)

```json
{
  "result": {
    "type": "success"
  },
  "type": "telemetry_destination_test"
}
```

#### Parameters

```ts
/** ID of the destination to test (starts with `tdst_`). */
destinationID: string; // path parameter

interface TelemetryDestinationTestParams {
  /** This endpoint is in beta: requests must send `telemetry-destinations-2026-08-11` in this header. */
  betas?: Array<AnthropicBeta>; // header parameter
}
```

#### Returns

```ts
/** The result of one test span sent to a destination. */
interface BetaTelemetryDestinationTestResponse {
  type: "telemetry_destination_test";
  /** How the test went: `success` when the destination answered with a 2xx status, else `failure` with the reason. */
  result: BetaTelemetryDestinationTestResult;
}
```

#### Types

```ts
type BetaTelemetryDestinationTestResult = BetaTelemetryDestinationTestSuccess | BetaTelemetryDestinationTestFailure;

/** The destination answered the test span with a 2xx status. */
interface BetaTelemetryDestinationTestSuccess {
  type: "success";
}

/** The test span was not delivered. */
interface BetaTelemetryDestinationTestFailure {
  type: "failure";
  /** A message that describes why the test span was not delivered, including the HTTP status code when the destination returned one. Examples: `HTTP error (status 403)`, `timeout`, `TLS failure`. It has the same form as the destination's `delivery_health.last_error` and never contains the destination's response body, any header value, a network address, or TLS details. */
  error: string;
}
```

### Add a Telemetry Destination Workspace

- Signature: `client.beta.organization.telemetryDestinations.workspaces.add(workspaceID: string, params: WorkspaceAddParams, options?: RequestOptions): BetaTelemetryDestinationWorkspace`

- Beta header: `anthropic-beta: telemetry-destinations-2026-08-11`

Add one workspace to a destination's workspace list.

Under `include` the workspace's spans start going to the destination. Under `exclude` they stop. A list holds at most 1,000 workspaces.

```ts
    destination_id: "destination_id"
  });
```

## Beta › Organization › Webhooks

### Create Organization Webhook Endpoint

- Signature: `client.beta.organization.webhooks.create(params: WebhookCreateParams, options?: RequestOptions): BetaNewOrganizationWebhookEndpoint`
- Endpoint: `POST /v1/organizations/webhooks`
- Beta header: `anthropic-beta: webhooks-2026-10-07`

Create an organization webhook endpoint.

An organization webhook endpoint belongs to the organization rather than to one of its workspaces. An organization can have at most 32 organization
webhook endpoints, enabled or disabled.

The response includes the endpoint's signing secret. No read returns it, so store
it when you receive it.

Every request must include the beta header `anthropic-beta: webhooks-2026-10-07`. A request without it returns `404`, exactly as if this API did not exist. Anthropic turns organization webhook endpoints on for each organization; until yours is on, requests also return `404`. Organization webhook endpoints are in beta and are not available to organizations with HIPAA readiness enabled.

```ts
import Anthropic from "@anthropic-ai/sdk";

});

const betaNewOrganizationWebhookEndpoint = await client.beta.organization.webhooks.create({
  enabled_events: ["user_profile.enforcement_action_opened"],
  url: "x"
});

console.log(betaNewOrganizationWebhookEndpoint.id);
```

```json
  "disabled_reason": "disabled_reason",

    "user_profile.enforcement_action_opened"

  "signing_secret": "signing_secret",

  "updated_at": "2019-12-27T18:11:19.117Z",
  "url": "url"
```
```ts
}
```

### Update Organization Webhook Endpoint

- Endpoint: `POST /v1/organizations/webhooks/{webhook_endpoint_id}`
- Beta header: `anthropic-beta: webhooks-2026-10-07`

Update an organization webhook endpoint. Only the fields you send are changed.

Every request must include the beta header `anthropic-beta: webhooks-2026-10-07`. A request without it returns `404`, exactly as if this API did not exist. Anthropic turns organization webhook endpoints on for each organization; until yours is on, requests also return `404`. Organization webhook endpoints are in beta and are not available to organizations with HIPAA readiness enabled.

```ts
);
```

```json
    "user_profile.enforcement_action_opened"
```

## Beta › Organization › Claude Tag › Slack Channels

### Set Up Slack Channel

- Signature: `client.beta.organization.claudeTag.slackChannels.create(params: SlackChannelCreateParams, options?: RequestOptions): BetaClaudeTagSlackChannel`
- Endpoint: `POST /v1/organizations/claude_tag/slack_channels`
- Beta header: `anthropic-beta: experimental-claude-tag-2026-10-21`

Set a Slack channel up for Claude Tag and return it with its identifier. If the channel is already set up, whether in claude.ai, by Claude's first use in it or by an earlier request, the existing channel is returned, so the request can be repeated. `settings`, when sent, is applied as an update applies it. Before a channel is set up, Claude's Slack app confirms with Slack that the channel is in the workspace, is not archived and is visible to the app; a channel that fails the confirmation returns 404. Setting the channel up and applying `settings` are two steps: when the second is refused, the response is the refusal, the channel stays set up with every setting unset, and the error's `details.slack_channel_id` holds the channel's identifier.

#### Example request

```ts
import Anthropic from "@anthropic-ai/sdk";

const client = new Anthropic({
  apiKey: process.env["ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"] // This is the default and can be omitted
});

const betaClaudeTagSlackChannel =
  await client.beta.organization.claudeTag.slackChannels.create({
    slack: { channel_id: "xx", workspace_id: "xx" }
  });

console.log(betaClaudeTagSlackChannel.id);
```

#### Example response (200)

```json
{
  "id": "id",
  "created_at": "2019-12-27T18:11:19.117Z",
  "settings": {
    "enabled": true,
    "environment_id": "environment_id",
    "guest_policy": {
      "type": "allow"
    },
    "instructions": "instructions",
    "model": "model",
    "reply_mode": {
      "type": "automatic"
    }
  },
  "slack": {
    "channel_id": "xx",
    "workspace_id": "xx"
  },
  "sources": {
    "enabled": {
      "slack_channel_id": "slack_channel_id",
      "type": "slack_channel"
    },
    "environment_id": {
      "slack_channel_id": "slack_channel_id",
      "type": "slack_channel"
    },
    "guest_policy": {
      "slack_channel_id": "slack_channel_id",
      "type": "slack_channel"
    },
    "instructions": [
      {
        "slack_channel_id": "slack_channel_id",
        "type": "slack_channel"
      }
    ],

      "type": "slack_channel"
    },

```

#### Parameters

```ts
interface SlackChannelCreateParams {
  /** Slack's own identifiers for the channel to set up. The organization must own the workspace. */
  slack: BetaClaudeTagSlackChannelIdentifiers;
  /** Settings to store on the channel, applied as Update Slack Channel applies them. */
  settings?: BetaClaudeTagSettingsCreate;
  /** This endpoint is in beta: requests must send `experimental-claude-tag-2026-10-21` in this header. */
  betas?: Array<AnthropicBeta>; // header parameter
}
```

#### Returns

```ts
/** A Slack channel set up for Claude Tag, with the settings it stores or, with `include_inherited`, the settings that apply in it. */
interface BetaClaudeTagSlackChannel {
  type: "slack_channel";
  /** The channel's identifier. Starts with `slch_`. It does not change for as long as the channel is set up, with one exception: a channel that is not configured can get a new one. A channel that is removed and set up again also has a new one. The old one keeps returning 404; look the channel up by its Slack identifiers for the new one. */
  id: string;
  /** Time the channel was set up, by whichever route. It does not change for as long as `id` does not. */
  created_at: string; // format: date-time
  /** What the channel itself stores or, with `include_inherited`, what applies in it. `sources` says which. */
  settings: BetaClaudeTagSettings;
  /** Slack's own identifiers for the channel. */
  slack: BetaClaudeTagSlackChannelIdentifiers;
  /** For each setting, the settings level its value in `settings` comes from. */
  sources: BetaClaudeTagSettingSources;
  /** Time Claude Tag's record of the channel last changed. It moves on every change to a setting, and can also move when something no response holds changes, so a later value says to read the channel again, not that a setting changed. Attaching or detaching a Bundle does not by itself move it. */
  updated_at: string; // format: date-time
}
```

#### Errors

Any method can also return the general [HTTP errors](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/errors?sdk_languages=typescript).

- `BetaSlackChannelSetUpSettingsRefusedError` (HTTP status 400, error code `slack_channel_set_up_settings_refused`)

  The request set the channel up, and `settings` was then refused. The channel stays set up with every setting unset.

- `BetaAPIKeyScopeMissingError` (HTTP status 403, error code `api_key_scope_missing`)

  The API key lacks the scope the request needs: `read:claude_tag` for a read, `write:claude_tag` for a change.

- `BetaClaudeTagWritesNotEnabledError` (HTTP status 403, error code `claude_tag_writes_not_enabled`)

  Changes through the Claude Tag API are not enabled for the organization.

- `BetaComplianceConfigurationRestrictedError` (HTTP status 403, error code `compliance_configuration_restricted`)

  The organization's compliance configuration does not let Claude Tag store anything new.

- `BetaOrganizationLevelScopedAPIKeyRequiredError` (HTTP status 403, error code `organization_level_scoped_api_key_required`)

  The credential is not a scoped API key that is bound at the organization level.

- `BetaEnvironmentNotFoundError` (HTTP status 404, error code `environment_not_found`)

  `settings.environment_id` names no Environment within the organization's reach.

- `BetaSlackChannelSetUpEnvironmentNotFoundError` (HTTP status 404, error code `slack_channel_set_up_environment_not_found`)

  `settings.environment_id` names no Environment within the organization's reach, and the request had set the channel up by then. The channel stays set up with every setting unset.

- `BetaSlackChannelSetUpSettingsConflictError` (HTTP status 409, error code `slack_channel_set_up_settings_conflict`)

  The request set the channel up, and something else then changed the channel or removed it. Nothing of `settings` was stored.

#### Types

```ts
interface BetaClaudeTagSlackChannelIdentifiers {
  /** Slack's identifier for the channel, starting with `C` or `G`, such as `C0456EFGH`. */
  channel_id: string; // minLength: 2, maxLength: 32
  /** Slack's identifier for the workspace the channel is in, starting with `T`, such as `T0123ABCD`. */
  workspace_id: string; // minLength: 2, maxLength: 32
}

interface BetaClaudeTagSettingsCreate {
  /** Whether Claude is on. `true` on a channel turns Claude on in it even when its workspace stores `false`. Null clears it. */
  enabled?: boolean | null;
  /** The environment Claude's sessions run in: the identifier of an active environment of the organization, starting with `env_`, or of a self-hosted runner pool of the organization that every member may use, starting with `ccpool_`. Null clears it. */
  environment_id?: string | null; // minLength: 1, maxLength: 64
  /** What Claude does in a channel while a Slack guest is in it. Null clears it. */
  guest_policy?: BetaClaudeTagGuestPolicy | null;
  /** Instructions for Claude, up to 8,192 characters after leading and trailing white space is trimmed. Null or blank text clears them. */
  instructions?: string | null;
  /** The model Claude uses: the identifier of a model, or the name of a model line, that the organization is entitled to for Claude Tag. Null clears it. */
  model?: string | null; // minLength: 1, maxLength: 128
  /** How Claude takes part in the channel: `automatic`, `mention_only`, `always_awake` or `thread`. Only a channel takes one: an update of a workspace that sends a value is refused, and one that sends null changes nothing. Null never clears it: sent to a channel that stores none it changes nothing, and sent to a channel that stores one it is refused, because a stored reply mode can be changed but never cleared; a caller that wants Claude's default behavior sends `automatic`. */
  reply_mode?: BetaClaudeTagReplyMode | null;
}

interface BetaClaudeTagSettings {
  /** Whether Claude is on. The nearest settings level that sets it decides. */
  enabled: boolean | null;
  /** The environment Claude's sessions run in, starting with `env_`, or the identifier of a self-hosted runner pool, starting with `ccpool_`. The nearest settings level that sets it decides. */
  environment_id: string | null;
  /** What Claude does in a channel while a Slack guest is in it. The nearest settings level that sets it decides. */
  guest_policy: BetaClaudeTagGuestPolicy | null;
  /** Instructions for Claude. Instructions add up: the text of every settings level that sets it is joined, broadest first. */
  instructions: string | null;
  /** The model Claude uses: a model identifier or the name of a model line. The nearest settings level that sets it decides. When none does, Claude uses the product's default model. */
  model: string | null;
  /** How Claude takes part in the channel. Only a channel stores one, and no settings level passes one on, so it is always null on a workspace. Null on a channel means the channel stores none yet: Claude then follows the reply mode chosen in Slack, if one was, else `automatic`. A stored reply mode can be changed but never cleared. */
  reply_mode: BetaClaudeTagReplyMode | null;
}

interface BetaClaudeTagSettingSources {
  /** The settings level `enabled` comes from. */
  enabled: BetaClaudeTagSettingSource | null;
  /** The settings level `environment_id` comes from. */
  environment_id: BetaClaudeTagSettingSource | null;
  /** The settings level `guest_policy` comes from. */
  guest_policy: BetaClaudeTagSettingSource | null;
  /** Every settings level that contributes text to `instructions`, broadest first, in the order their text is joined. Empty when none does. */
  instructions: Array<BetaClaudeTagSettingSource>;
  /** The settings level `model` comes from. */
  model: BetaClaudeTagSettingSource | null;
  /** The settings level `reply_mode` comes from: the channel when it stores one. With `include_inherited=true` and no stored mode it is `default`. */
  reply_mode: BetaClaudeTagSettingSource | null;
}

type BetaClaudeTagGuestPolicy = BetaClaudeTagGuestPolicyAllow | BetaClaudeTagGuestPolicyRestrict | BetaClaudeTagGuestPolicyChannelOnly;

type BetaClaudeTagReplyMode = BetaClaudeTagReplyModeAutomatic | BetaClaudeTagReplyModeMentionOnly | BetaClaudeTagReplyModeAlwaysAwake | BetaClaudeTagReplyModeThread;

/** Claude answers in the channel. */
interface BetaClaudeTagGuestPolicyAllow {
  type: "allow";
}

/** Claude does not answer in the channel. */
interface BetaClaudeTagGuestPolicyRestrict {
  type: "restrict";
}

/** Claude answers with only the Bundles attached to the channel itself. */
interface BetaClaudeTagGuestPolicyChannelOnly {
  type: "channel_only";
}

/** Claude reads along and joins in when it can help, and pauses on its own in quiet or busy channels. */
interface BetaClaudeTagReplyModeAutomatic {
  type: "automatic";
}

/** Claude replies only when it is @-mentioned. */
interface BetaClaudeTagReplyModeMentionOnly {
  type: "mention_only";
}

/** Like `automatic`, but Claude never pauses on its own. Available where it is enabled for the channel. */
interface BetaClaudeTagReplyModeAlwaysAwake {
  type: "always_awake";
}

/** Every new top-level message in the channel gets its own reply from Claude, in a thread under it. Available where it is enabled for the channel, and only once Claude has been used in the channel. */
interface BetaClaudeTagReplyModeThread {
  type: "thread";
}

type BetaClaudeTagSettingSource = BetaClaudeTagSlackChannelSettingSource | BetaClaudeTagSlackWorkspaceSettingSource | BetaClaudeTagSlackParentChannelSettingSource | BetaClaudeTagSlackDefaultSettingSource | BetaClaudeTagDefaultSettingSource | BetaClaudeTagSlackGridChannelSettingSource;

/** The value comes from the addressed Slack channel itself. */
interface BetaClaudeTagSlackChannelSettingSource {
  type: "slack_channel";
  /** The channel's identifier, starting with `slch_`. */
  slack_channel_id: string;
}

/** The value comes from a Slack workspace of the organization. */
interface BetaClaudeTagSlackWorkspaceSettingSource {
  type: "slack_workspace";
  /** The workspace's identifier, starting with `slws_`. */
  slack_workspace_id: string;
}

/** The value comes from the channel that a code channel was started from. A parent channel contributes `instructions` and `environment_id` only. */
interface BetaClaudeTagSlackParentChannelSettingSource {
  type: "slack_parent_channel";
  /** The parent channel's identifier, starting with `slch_`. */
  slack_channel_id: string;
}

/** The value comes from the organization's Slack defaults, which have no identifier. */
interface BetaClaudeTagSlackDefaultSettingSource {
  type: "slack_default";
}

/** No settings level sets a value, and the built-in default applies. */
interface BetaClaudeTagDefaultSettingSource {
  type: "default";
}

/** The value comes from the addressed channel as it is set up under another workspace of its Enterprise Grid: a channel shared across the Grid keeps one Slack channel identifier in every workspace that sees it. */
interface BetaClaudeTagSlackGridChannelSettingSource {
  type: "slack_grid_channel";
  /** Slack's own identifiers for the channel under that other workspace. */
  slack: BetaClaudeTagSlackChannelIdentifiers;
}
```

### List Slack Channels

- Signature: `client.beta.organization.claudeTag.slackChannels.list(params: SlackChannelListParams, options?: RequestOptions): PageCursor<BetaClaudeTagSlackChannel>`
- Endpoint: `GET /v1/organizations/claude_tag/slack_channels`
- Beta header: `anthropic-beta: experimental-claude-tag-2026-10-21`

List the set-up Slack channels of one Slack workspace, newest first by `created_at`. A channel that is not set up is not listed: Slack holds the full list of a workspace's channels. Pass `slack_channel_id` as well to look one channel up by its Slack identifiers: `data` then holds that channel, or is empty when it is not set up, and `limit` and `page` are ignored. A workspace that the organization owns only through a Slack Enterprise Grid returns 404 until it is set up. With `include_inherited=true` each channel's `settings` holds what applies in it, and the request fails with 503 rather than resolve against a settings level that could not be read. A `page` cursor resumes only a request with the same `include_inherited`.

```ts
import Anthropic from "@anthropic-ai/sdk";

const client = new Anthropic({
  apiKey: process.env["ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"] // This is the default and can be omitted
});

// Automatically fetches more pages as needed.
for await (const betaClaudeTagSlackChannel of client.beta.organization.claudeTag.slackChannels.list(
  { slack_workspace_id: "slack_workspace_id" }
)) {
  console.log(betaClaudeTagSlackChannel.id);
}
```

```ts
interface SlackChannelListParams {
```

### Get Slack Channel

- Signature: `client.beta.organization.claudeTag.slackChannels.retrieve(id: string, params?: SlackChannelRetrieveParams, options?: RequestOptions): BetaClaudeTagSlackChannel`
- Endpoint: `GET /v1/organizations/claude_tag/slack_channels/{id}`
- Beta header: `anthropic-beta: experimental-claude-tag-2026-10-21`

Get one Slack channel and its settings. By default `settings` holds what the channel itself stores: a setting that is null there is not set on the channel and is inherited. With `include_inherited=true`, `settings` holds what applies in the channel once the settings levels above it are taken into account, and the request fails with 503 rather than resolve against a settings level that could not be read. Either way `sources` names the settings level each value comes from, so a caller tells the channel's own value from an inherited one by its source, not by whether it is null.

```ts
  await client.beta.organization.claudeTag.slackChannels.retrieve(
    "slch_01SvpyRQK3nN6eH9uhRA7n1q"

console.log(betaClaudeTagSlackChannel.id);
```

### Update Slack Channel

```ts
interface BetaClaudeTagSettingsUpdate {
  /** Whether Claude is on. `true` on a channel turns Claude on in it even when its workspace stores `false`. Null clears it. */
  enabled?: boolean | null;
  /** The environment Claude's sessions run in: the identifier of an active environment of the organization, starting with `env_`, or of a self-hosted runner pool of the organization that every member may use, starting with `ccpool_`. Null clears it. */
  environment_id?: string | null; // minLength: 1, maxLength: 64
  /** What Claude does in a channel while a Slack guest is in it. Null clears it. */
  guest_policy?: BetaClaudeTagGuestPolicy | null;
  /** Instructions for Claude, up to 8,192 characters after leading and trailing white space is trimmed. Null or blank text clears them. */
  instructions?: string | null;
  /** The model Claude uses: the identifier of a model, or the name of a model line, that the organization is entitled to for Claude Tag. Null clears it. */
  model?: string | null; // minLength: 1, maxLength: 128
  /** How Claude takes part in the channel: `automatic`, `mention_only`, `always_awake` or `thread`. Only a channel takes one: an update of a workspace that sends a value is refused, and one that sends null changes nothing. Null never clears it: sent to a channel that stores none it changes nothing, and sent to a channel that stores one it is refused, because a stored reply mode can be changed but never cleared; a caller that wants Claude's default behavior sends `automatic`. */
  reply_mode?: BetaClaudeTagReplyMode | null;
}
```

### Remove Slack Channel

- Signature: `client.beta.organization.claudeTag.slackChannels.delete(id: string, params?: SlackChannelDeleteParams, options?: RequestOptions): BetaClaudeTagDeletedSlackChannel`
- Endpoint: `DELETE /v1/organizations/claude_tag/slack_channels/{id}`
- Beta header: `anthropic-beta: experimental-claude-tag-2026-10-21`

Remove a Slack channel from Claude Tag. This deletes the channel's stored settings and its Bundle Targets at once, and then, in the background, the channel's sessions and their transcripts, its memory, its routines and the artifacts published from it. None of it can be restored. The channel in Slack and its messages are unchanged. The request is refused with 400 and `error.details.error_code` `slack_channel_enabled` while `enabled` resolves to `true` for the channel, as a read with `include_inherited=true` returns it: set `enabled` to `false` on the channel first. This guards against removing a channel in use by mistake; it is not a way to keep Claude out, because the removal deletes the channel's own `enabled: false` with its other settings, after which the channel inherits again and Claude's next use of it can set it up anew with a new identifier. The identifier returns 404 as soon as the request returns, so a repeated removal returns 404. A group direct message returns 400, and so does a channel that holds configuration this API does not manage.

#### Example request

```ts
import Anthropic from "@anthropic-ai/sdk";

const client = new Anthropic({
  apiKey: process.env["ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"] // This is the default and can be omitted
});

const betaClaudeTagDeletedSlackChannel =
  await client.beta.organization.claudeTag.slackChannels.delete(
    "slch_01SvpyRQK3nN6eH9uhRA7n1q"
  );

console.log(betaClaudeTagDeletedSlackChannel.id);
```

#### Example response (200)

```json
{
  "id": "id",
  "type": "slack_channel_deleted"
}
```

```ts
  /** This endpoint is in beta: requests must send `experimental-claude-tag-2026-10-21` in this header. */
  betas?: Array<AnthropicBeta>; // header parameter
}
```

#### Returns

```ts

interface BetaClaudeTagDeletedSlackChannel {
  type: "slack_channel_deleted";
  /** The removed channel's identifier. */
  id: string;
}
```

```ts
  /** The workspace's identifier. Starts with `slws_`. It does not change for as long as the workspace is set up. A workspace that is removed and set up again has a new one, and the old one keeps returning 404; look the workspace up by its Slack identifier for the new one. */

  sources: BetaClaudeTagSettingSources;

}
```

### Attach Bundle

- Signature: `client.beta.organization.claudeTag.bundles.targets.create(bundleID: string, params: TargetCreateParams, options?: RequestOptions): BetaClaudeTagBundleTarget`
- Endpoint: `POST /v1/organizations/claude_tag/bundles/{bundle_id}/targets`
- Beta header: `anthropic-beta: experimental-claude-tag-2026-10-21`

Attach a Bundle to a Slack channel or a Slack workspace. A Bundle attached to a workspace can be used in the workspace and in every channel in it. Attaching a Bundle to a channel or workspace it is already attached to returns the existing Bundle Target. The channel or workspace must be set up: attaching never sets a channel up. A group direct message takes no Bundle and returns 400.

```ts
  await client.beta.organization.claudeTag.bundles.targets.create(
    "capp_011CZkZjLP1cWxj5EtMmdgbq",
    { target: { slack_channel_id: "xxxxxxxx", type: "slack_channel" } }
  );

console.log(betaClaudeTagBundleTarget);
```
